subject: Clarifying billing buckets, per-request floors, and session aggregation
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pixeltail.ai>

Subject: Quick question on how you bill short multi-turn sessions

Hi Ben,

We're evaluating Redwood for in-app chat at PixelTail and I have a few quick billing questions before we run an eval:

- How do you treat very short multi-turn sessions (3–6 user messages, each ~10–30 tokens)? Is each request billed independently or can they be aggregated?
- Do you round up tokens to a bucket (and if so, what size)?
- For long-context prompts where we reuse a system prompt + KB prefix, do we get any cost credit for cached prefixes?

Attached a tiny sample request log so you can see our typical packet sizes. We're sensitive to per-request floors because our UX sends a short context for each user turn.

Thanks — would appreciate a short note so we can size costs for a pilot.

—Olivia
Olivia Chen

High-level answers up front: we bill input + output tokens, and we have configurable aggregation and a per-request floor for micro-traffic by default. - Do you expect the KB/system prompt to change frequently (every turn) or be stable across a user session?

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pixeltail.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on how you bill short multi-turn sessions

Hi Olivia — thanks for the log and Ben for the intros. Below is our standard behavior plus a few optional configurations that can materially affect cost for chat-style workloads. I'll keep this focused and numeric.

1) Base unit and measurement
- We count and bill input tokens + output tokens. Tokenization uses our standard tokenizer; numbers above are practical estimates, not sub-token rounding.

2) Per-request floor / bucket policy (default)
- Default behavior: we apply a per-request minimum charge of 32 tokens. Any request with fewer tokens is rounded up to 32 tokens. This prevents extreme overhead from tiny HTTP calls and the associated runtime cost.
- Billing granularity beyond the floor: tokens are recorded at 1-token granularity for requests >= 32 tokens.

3) Session aggregation (optional, recommended for chat UX)
- We offer a server-side session aggregation feature that will combine closely-timed requests from the same session into aggregation windows. Default window: 2.5 seconds. When enabled, multiple small turns submitted within the window are coalesced for billing and for batching to the runtime.
- When aggregated, the combined request is evaluated as a single billable call (subject to the per-request floor; i.e. aggregated size rounded up to 32 tokens if <32). This can eliminate repeated floor hits for rapid turn-taking.

4) Cached prefix treatment (KV/prefix caching)
- If you enable prefix/KV caching for a stable KB or system prompt, cached tokens are flagged at request time and billed at a reduced rate: cached tokens are billed at 20% of the standard per-token rate (we call this the "cached token surcharge").
- Practically: a 1,024-token stable prefix that is cached and reused across turns will be billed slice-by-slice only once at full price (first time to populate cache) and thereafter at 20% of the unit price when referenced.

5) Long-context and rolling windows
- For large prompts where the runtime needs to re-encode substantial context (outside of cacheable prefixes), you will be billed for the full active context length. We recommend trimming or using truncated retrieval when possible.

6) Exceptions and pilot-friendly options (negotiable)
- For pilot customers we can: (a) reduce the per-request floor to 8 tokens for specific routes, or (b) enable session-aggregation at the edge with a 3-second window and waive floor charges for aggregated calls. These are time-limited pilot concessions tied to a committed evaluation period.

7) Example math (from your log)
- Typical turn in your sample: ~18 input tokens + 12 output tokens = 30 tokens -> default billing = 32 tokens (floor).
- With aggregation (two turns within 2.5s): combined 60 tokens -> billed at 60 tokens (no floor).
- With a stable 512-token prefix cached: each turn will include the prefix reference but most of that will be billed at 20% after cache warmup.

If you want, I can run a short cost model for your projected monthly active users and turn frequency and attach a 12-month projection. Ben — should I share this directly with Olivia or coordinate via the HubSpot deal?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pixeltail.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on how you bill short multi-turn sessions

Thanks — that's very helpful, Laura. A few follow-ups and a quick ask: 

- For our pilot we expect many ~30-token turns at ~2s cadence for a single user session. The default 32-token floor will double our estimated cost unless aggregation is perfect. Can you confirm whether the aggregation window behaves correctly across mobile networks with intermittent latency?
- For the KB cache, the 20% surcharge after warmup sounds reasonable.

On commercial terms: we're interested in a 12-month committed volume if we can get two things: (1) a 30–40% unit discount at 250M tokens/month commit and (2) waiver of the per-request floor for routes where session aggregation is enabled (we can provide session ids). We also attached our initial redlines to speed contracting.

If you can sketch a counter-offer, we can escalate internally.

—Olivia

Attachment: contract_redlines_v1.pdf (45 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@pixeltail.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on how you bill short multi-turn sessions

Olivia — appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. We're excited about PixelTail as a pilot customer. Short answer / commercial counter-proposal: 

1) Pricing and discounting
- Commit: 250M tokens/month for 12 months.
- Unit discount: 30% off standard hosted per-token list price for both input and output tokens. Volume tiers above 400M/month would trigger higher discounts; let's revisit at Q3.

2) Per-request floor waiver for aggregated routes
- We'll waive the 32-token floor for specific routes where you emit a session_id and enable session-aggregation on the route. Requirements: session aggregation must be enabled on your account and calls must contain a session_id field to be eligible. Waiver held for the duration of the 12-month commit.

3) Aggregation behavior and mobile networks
- Our aggregation runs at the edge and is tolerant to small network jitter. The 2.5s window is configurable up to 5s for mobile use cases. If a request arrives outside the window it's billed separately. For mobile with intermittent latency we recommend a 3–4s window to reduce floor hits; I'll work with your eng team to validate in a short smoke test.

4) Cache/reference billing
- Confirming Laura's note: cached prefix references billed at 20% after warmup. We'll provide instrumentation so you can verify cache hit rates during the pilot.

Next steps
- Ben, can you lock a technical smoke test (10k calls) and a pricing SOW? Olivia, if you want, I can circulate a short amendment to your redlines reflecting the 30% discount + floor waiver for aggregated routes.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
VP Product, Redwood Inference
